# MDL302 · `trailing-whitespace-in-value`

<!-- Generated by tools/gendocs from internal/rules: do not edit. -->

A value ends with spaces or tabs, which GLib keeps.

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | values |
| Default severity | error |
| Fix | unsafe |
| Design references | K9, G5 |

## Why

GLib strips the spaces before a value but keeps those after it. An integer option such as `threads=4 ` then fails to parse and mydumper aborts at startup; a path such as `outputdir=/backup ` names a directory with a trailing space; a regular expression matches something else. The fix trims the value; it is unsafe because it changes what mydumper reads (promote it with `fix.extend-safe` when trailing spaces are never intended).

SQL-valued keys of table sections (`where`, `columns_on_select`, ...) are not checked: trailing spaces are harmless in SQL.

## Example

❌ Before:

```ini
[`db`.`t`]
where=a > 1 
limit=10 
```

```text
3:9-3:10 error MDL302[trailing-whitespace-in-value] the value of `limit` ends with whitespace, which GLib keeps
  = The whitespace becomes part of the value.
  fix (unsafe): Remove the trailing whitespace
```

✅ After `mydumper-lint check --fix --unsafe-fixes`:

```text
[`db`.`t`]
where=a > 1·
limit=10
```

(`\r`, `\t` and `\xHH` stand for the bytes they name, `·` for a trailing space)

## Configuration

Enabled by default. To change its severity or turn it off:

```yaml
rules:
  severity:
    MDL302: warning   # or error, info, off
```

To accept one occurrence, put `# mydumper-lint: disable-next-line=MDL302` on the line above it.
